intro: Haiti was the first country founded by formerly enslaved people, after the only successful large-scale slave revolution in history.

chapters.title: Saint-Domingue
text: The Taíno lived on the island of Hispaniola when Columbus arrived in 1492. France took the western part, Saint-Domingue, which by the 1780s was the world's richest colony, producing much of Europe's sugar and coffee with hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans.

chapters.title: The Haitian Revolution
text: In 1791 enslaved people rose up. Led by Toussaint Louverture and then Jean-Jacques Dessalines, they defeated French, Spanish and British armies. Haiti declared independence on 1 January 1804.

highlight.title: A world first
highlight.text: Haiti was the first Black republic and the first country in the Americas to abolish slavery for good.

chapters.title: A difficult history
text: In 1825 France forced Haiti to pay a huge 'indemnity' for its independence, a debt that crippled its economy for over a century. The US occupied Haiti from 1915 to 1934, and the Duvalier dictatorships ruled from 1957 to 1986.

A 2010 earthquake killed over 200,000 people. Since the president's assassination in 2021, armed gangs have taken control of most of the capital, and a Kenyan-led international security mission has been deployed.

keyTerms.meaning: The island shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
